thesis: The hard part of putting a robot on a fishing boat is already solved, and it is not the part anyone expects. The unsolved part is the boat.
long_form: A machine learning model finds the brain of each individual salmon, because the brain sits in a different place in every fish, which is why a jig cannot do this and a model must. That is real and was independently reported twice. What is not established is that any of it has reached Alaska. One trade write-up carries the entire Cook Inlet story, against more than thirteen hundred permits in that inlet alone.
valence_defense: Celebratory would overclaim an Alaska deployment nobody has confirmed. Cautionary would undersell engineering that two independent outlets verified two years apart. Curiosity is the only register that can hold a solved mechanism and an unconfirmed rollout at the same time, and it rotates off a wry run and a mixed one.
supporting_facts: c9 + c18: computer vision and machine learning locate the brain of each individual fish. Khawaja, verbatim: the brain can be in a different location. That sentence is the whole reason a model is needed.

c15 + c14: the company's own 2024 goal was ten machines in use company-wide, across all fisheries. Upper Cook Inlet alone holds more than 1,300 permits, about a tenth of every salmon permit in Alaska.
c19: exactly one trade write-up carries the Alaska story. No Alaska outlet and no fisheries trade outlet has covered it.
fair_counterpoint_that_gets_a_scene: This is exactly what a real pilot looks like on day one. One boat, one write-up, proof before scale. Demanding fleet-wide numbers from a seed-stage company's first Alaska mention is an unfair bar, and every genuine rollout in this fishery's history started smaller than its press release.
how_it_narrows_honestly: The film does not call the Alaska claim false. It says the record is one write-up, names what would settle it, and leaves the question open on screen.
the_lazy_angle_we_refuse: Robot comes for Alaska's fishermen. It is wrong on the facts: ike jime needs a trained hand and most small boats do not do it at all, so no job is being displaced. A skill that mostly was not there is being made reachable.
who_it_serves: A Cook Inlet permit holder who heard this secondhand now knows which half is engineering and which half is a press release, and what question to ask before believing it applies to their boat.
runners_up: SKEPTIC lens, pure sourcing story: rejected as the spine because a film whose subject is the thinness of a press release has no second movement and no mechanism to draw.
ENTHUSIAST lens, quality-at-capture as a small-boat lever: kept and grafted into Act 2, because it is the honest reason an Alaskan should care at all.
MECHANISM lens, automating access to a scarce hand skill: kept and grafted, and it supplies the refusal of the job-loss frame.
throughline_object: THE TARGET DOT, the point the machine picks behind a salmon's eye
